'''James Dugundji''' (August 30, 1919 – January 8, 1985) was an American mathematician, a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Southern California]].<ref name="mardesic">{{citation
 | last = Mardešić | first = Sibe
 | editor-first = Ioan Mackenzie | editor-last = James
 | contribution = Absolute neighborhood retracts and shape theory
 | doi = 10.1016/B978-044482375-5/50010-9
 | location = Amsterdam
 | mr = 1674915
 | pages = 241–269
 | publisher = North-Holland
 | title = History of Topology
 | year = 1999
 | isbn = 978-0-444-82375-5
 }}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=7iRijkz0rrUC&pg=PA244 p. 244] for a brief biography of Dugundji.</ref><ref name="granas">[http://journals.impan.pl/bc/PDF/bc77-0-001.pdf Note about the life and work of Dugundji] by Andrzej Granas in their book ''Fixed Point Theory'', Springer, 2005. Reprinted in {{harvtxt|Jachymski|Reich|2007}}, p. 9.</ref>

== Life ==
Dugundji's parents emigrated from [[Greece]] to [[New York City]], where Dugundji was born in 1919. He studied at [[New York University]], graduating with a B.A. in 1940, and went on to graduate school at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], studying there under the supervision of [[Witold Hurewicz]]. After two years of study at UNC, Dugundji joined the [[United States Air Force]] for the duration of [[World War II]], and then completed his doctorate from 1946 to 1948 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], to which his advisor had moved. He then took a faculty position at the University of Southern California, where he remained for the rest of his career. He was also a long-time member of the editorial boards of two mathematics journals, the ''[[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]]'' and ''[[Topology and its Applications]]''.<ref name="mardesic"/><ref name="granas"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=246}}</ref>

Dugundji is the author of the textbook ''Topology'' (Allyn and Bacon, 1966), on [[general topology]]. Reviewer M. Edelstein wrote that this was "one of the best among the numerous books on the subject",<ref>Review of ''Topology'' by M. Edelstein, {{MR|0193606}}.</ref> and it went through numerous reprintings.<ref>Twelfth reprinting of ''Topology'', Allyn and Bacon, 1978, {{ISBN|0-205-00271-4}}, {{MR|0478089}}.</ref> With Andrzej Granas he also wrote the research monograph ''Fixed Point Theory''; originally planned as a two-volume series, the first volume was published by [[Polish Scientific Publishers PWN|Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe]] in 1982, and the complete text was published as a single volume in 2003 by [[Springer-Verlag]].<ref>Review of Fixed Point Theory, I, Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe, 1982, by Christian Fenske, {{MR|0660439}}.</ref><ref name="kartsatos">Review of Fixed Point Theory, Springer-Verlag, 2005, by A. G. Kartsatos, {{MR|1987179}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Brown, Robert F.|title=Review: ''Fixed point theory'', by Andrzej Granas and James Dugundji|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|year=2004|volume=41|issue=2|pages=267–271|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/2004-41-02/S0273-0979-04-01008-0/ | doi = 10.1090/S0273-0979-04-01008-0|doi-access=free}}</ref> Reviewer A. G. Kartsatos called the completed volume "the most comprehensive, well-written and complete book on [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed point theory]] to date".<ref name="kartsatos"/>

In his own research, as well as producing highly cited works on problems of pure mathematics such as the [[Tietze extension theorem]],<ref>{{citation
 | last = Dugundji | first = J.
 | journal = Pacific Journal of Mathematics
 | mr = 0044116
 | pages = 353–367
 | title = An extension of Tietze's theorem
 | volume = 1
 | year = 1951
 | issue = 3
 | doi=10.2140/pjm.1951.1.353| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> Dugundji did important early work in [[cheminformatics]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Dugundji | first1 = James
 | last2 = Ugi | first2 = Ivar | author2-link = Ivar Karl Ugi
 | contribution = An algebraic model of constitutional chemistry as a basis for chemical computer programs
 | doi = 10.1007/BFb0051317
 | pages = 19–64
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | series = Topics in Current Chemistry
 | title = Computers in Chemistry
 | volume = 39/1
 | year = 1973
 | isbn = 3-540-06231-9
 }}.</ref> With co-authors [[Ivar Karl Ugi|I. Ugi]], R. Kopp and D. Marquarding, he wrote a book on this subject as well, ''Perspectives in Theoretical Stereochemistry'' (Springer, 1984).<ref name="granas"/>

In 2005, an international conference on fixed point theorems was held in Dugundji's memory in [[Będlewo]], [[Poland]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Jachymski | first1 = Jacek
 | last2 = Reich | first2 = Simeon
 | editor1-first = Jacek
 | editor1-last = Jachymski
 | editor2-first = Simeon
 | editor2-last = Reich
 | doi = 10.4064/bc77
 | location = Warsaw
 | mr = 2341373
 | publisher = Polish Academy of Sciences Institute of Mathematics
 | series = Banach Center Publications
 | title = Fixed Point Theory and its Applications: Proceedings of the International Conference dedicated to the memory of Professor James Dugundji, held in Będlewo, August 1–5, 2005
 | volume = 77
 | year = 2007}}.</ref>
